messages:
maya: Quick design run — thinking about the initial journey for new accounts. Current idea: compact 'Get set up' checklist in the dashboard header vs. a persistent sample-projects carousel. Screenshot: https://redwood-internal/s/figma/abc123 :eyes:

ria (Product Design): I prefer a compact checklist. Fewer choices up front -> higher completion. Suggestion: 3 primary steps (Connect API key, Launch sample project, Add billing). Make the sample projects secondary CTA beneath checklist.

kevin (FE): Layout note: carousel is heavy on DOM and hurts initial paint on low-bandwidth. If we keep projects visible, lazy-load images and render as static cards (no autoplay). Also put aria-hidden on decorative images.

patrick (PM): Metrics: target 10% uplift in setup completion week1. We should A/B test checklist (A) vs. banner + modal (B). Track events: setup.started, sample.opened, setup.completed.

elena (DevEx): Microcopy tweaks: replace "Add billing" with "Enable billing for production" — feels clearer. For sample projects CTA, use "Launch sample" not "Try" — more action-oriented. Keep tone short and dev-friendly.

ria (Product Design): Accessibility nits: keyboard focus order needs to be linear — checklist items should be tabbable and not skip when modal opens. Also visible focus state for the CTA buttons (avoid relying solely on color).

a11y-bot: Accessibility check: color contrast scan failed on primary CTA (#6a5acd on #ffffff) — ratio 3:1. Must be 4.5:1 for body text. Recommend darker purple or add 2px outline for focus.

kevin (FE): Quick code snippet for accessible CTA I can put in the prototype:
```html
<button class="primary" aria-label="Launch sample project: Todo app">Launch sample</button>
```
Make sure `aria-expanded` toggles when the sample modal opens.

maya: Design tradeoff question — do we gate sample projects behind a modal (cleaner header) or keep inline cards (faster access)? leaning modal to reduce clutter on first page.

patrick (PM): Modal wins for tracking (we can measure opens) and reduces initial cognitive load. But make modal dismissible and persist "seen" state so returning users don't see it again. Add a small "Remind me later" option.

ria (Product Design): If modal, include a very small on-dashboard hint (icon + "Samples") so users who skip can get back. Use plain language: "Open sample projects".

elena (DevEx): Copy variants to A/B test:
- Variant A: "Launch a sample project — try an end-to-end request in seconds."
- Variant B: "Explore a sample project — see Redwood serving in <2 minutes."
Also propose inline tooltips for first-run steps with keyboard shortcuts.

maya: OK — action items:
1) Ria to update mockup with modal + dashboard hint (due EOD Wed).
2) Kevin implement lightweight prototype (no carousel, lazy images) for perf test.
3) Patrick to set up analytics events and A/B flags.
4) Elena to draft two microcopy variants for experiment.
5) Ria + Kevin to address a11y-bot contrast + focus states.

kevin (FE): :thumbsup: will prototype and add notes in PR about lazy-loading and `aria-expanded`.

ria (Product Design): Noted. I'll also add a simplified checklist view for mobile — one column, collapsible.

maya: Thanks all. Scheduling 15-min follow-up tomorrow 9:30 to review mocks. If anyone has objections to modal path, shout now. :smile:

patrick (PM): No objections. If completion dips, we revert to inline cards.

kevin (FE): quick perf FYI — if images are >200KB each, they kill First Contentful Paint on 3G. Use SVG placeholders or 8-bit blurred previews.

a11y-bot: Reminder: add `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` to modal container and trap focus when open.

maya: Good call. I'll add that to the mock. End of thread.
